pharm: Selective imidazoline I1-receptor agonist; reduces central sympathetic outflow
summary: Moxonidine is a centrally acting antihypertensive and selective imidazoline I1-receptor agonist used for mild to moderate essential hypertension. It lowers blood pressure by reducing central sympathetic outflow, with fewer sedative and dry-mouth effects than older central agents like clonidine. It is not FDA-approved; use is based on European SmPC/BNF. The usual starting dose is 0.2 mg once daily, increased if needed to a maximum of 0.6 mg/day in divided doses.

dosage.d: Increase after 3 weeks to 0.4 mg/day if needed, given once daily or in two divided doses

dosage.n: Do not exceed 0.4 mg as a single dose or 0.6 mg/day total

dosage.d: Single dose not exceeding 0.2 mg, total not exceeding 0.4 mg/day

admin: Take once daily, usually in the morning, with or without food
Titrate at intervals of about 3 weeks based on response
Do not stop abruptly; taper over about 2 weeks to avoid rebound hypertension
If used with a beta-blocker, stop the beta-blocker first, then moxonidine, when discontinuing both
moa: Selective agonist at central imidazoline I1 receptors (with weaker alpha-2 adrenoceptor activity) in the rostral ventrolateral medulla, reducing sympathetic nervous system outflow and thereby lowering peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure.

absolute: Sick sinus syndrome or second-/third-degree AV block
Severe coronary artery disease or unstable angina
relative: Severe coronary artery disease / recent myocardial infarction
Intermittent claudication, Raynaud phenomenon, Parkinson disease, epilepsy, glaucoma, depression

preg: Safety not established; avoid unless clearly necessary.
lact: Excreted in human milk; avoid during breastfeeding or discontinue nursing.
renal: Renally cleared; reduce dose in moderate impairment (single dose <=0.2 mg, total <=0.4 mg/day) and avoid if eGFR <30 mL/min.
hepatic: Use with caution; data limited, particularly in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Tricyclic antidepressants — may reduce the antihypertensive effect
moderate: Sedatives, benzodiazepines, alcohol — additive CNS depression
Beta-blockers — additive bradycardia and rebound risk on withdrawal
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.

emergency: Hypertensive rebound crisis after sudden stop

monitoring: Renal function before and during therapy
Symptoms of dizziness, sedation or depression
counsel: Take once daily as prescribed; do not stop suddenly
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness, especially at first
Avoid alcohol and use caution with driving until you know how it affects you
Dry mouth is common and usually improves
Tell your doctor about heart-rhythm problems or other blood-pressure medicines
pearls: Not FDA-approved; dosing and safety per European SmPC / BNF
Selective imidazoline I1 agonist — fewer sedation/dry-mouth effects than clonidine
Do not stop abruptly: taper to avoid rebound hypertension
When discontinuing alongside a beta-blocker, stop the beta-blocker first
Contraindicated in significant bradyarrhythmias and severe heart failure
missed: Take as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not double up. Resume the usual once-daily schedule.
overdose: Expect sedation, marked hypotension, bradycardia and dry mouth (paradoxical hypertension possible early). Provide supportive care and fluids; atropine for symptomatic bradycardia; vasopressors for hypotension. No specific antidote.
